excerpts.text: Third quarter net income attributable to Deere & Company was $811 million... compared with $899 million... net sales and revenues decreased 11%, to $8.925 billion... Diluted earnings per share were $2.57 compared with $2.81.

Net income attributable to Deere & Company is forecast to be about $2.25 billion for the full year... Agriculture and Turf division's worldwide sales are forecast to decline about 10 percent for fiscal year 2020... Construction and Forestry sales are anticipated to be down about 25 percent for 2020.
The company has announced broad employee-separation programs that will be completed during the fourth quarter... about $175 million in pretax charges... an estimated $175 million in annual savings.

Agriculture and Turf: net sales of $5.672 billion, down 5%; operating profit of $942 million, up from $612 million a year earlier. Construction and Forestry: net sales of $2.187 billion, down 28%; operating profit of $205 million, down from $378 million. Financial Services: net income attributable to Deere & Company of $183 million, up from $175 million.

U.S. and Canada industry sales of large agricultural equipment are forecast to be down 5 to 10 percent... Europe is projected to be down 5 to 10 percent... South America is forecast to be down 10 to 15 percent... Industry sales of construction equipment in North America are expected to decline about 20 percent... Global forestry industry sales are forecast to be down 20 to 25 percent.

Deere's number-one priority continues to be safeguarding the health and well-being of its employees... unsettled market conditions and related customer uncertainty are expected to have a moderating effect on key markets in the near term.

Nine months net cash provided by operating activities was $4,057 million compared with $404 million; purchases of property and equipment were $594 million compared with $756 million; dividends paid were $718 million compared with $703 million; a quarterly dividend of $0.76 per share was declared, unchanged from a year earlier; share repurchases totaled $263 million for the first nine months of 2020 compared with $880 million a year earlier.

claims.text: Deere designs, manufactures and distributes agricultural, turf-care, and construction and forestry equipment worldwide, sold mainly through independent dealers, and also provides retail and wholesale financing for that equipment and other assets through its financial services segment; revenue is earned primarily from equipment sales, with additional revenue from financing income and services.

Third-quarter fiscal 2020 net sales and revenues fell 11% to $8.925 billion, with net income of $811 million ($2.57 per diluted share), down from $899 million ($2.81 per diluted share) a year earlier.

Management forecast full-year fiscal 2020 net income of about $2.25 billion, with worldwide Agriculture and Turf equipment sales expected down about 10% and Construction and Forestry sales expected down about 25% for the year.

The company announced broad employee-separation programs to be completed in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2020, carrying about $175 million of pretax charges and an estimated $175 million in annual cost savings.

By segment in the third quarter: Agriculture and Turf net sales fell 5% to $5.672 billion while operating profit rose to $942 million (16.6% margin) from $612 million (10.3% margin); Construction and Forestry net sales fell 28% to $2.187 billion while operating profit fell to $205 million (9.4% margin) from $378 million (12.5% margin); Financial Services net income rose to $183 million from $175 million.

Management's industry forecasts called for U.S./Canada large agricultural equipment sales down 5-10%, Europe down 5-10% and South America down 10-15%, alongside North America construction equipment sales down about 20% and global forestry sales down 20-25%.

Management said its top priority remained safeguarding employee health during the pandemic, crediting early safety measures with keeping factories and parts centers functioning, while cautioning that unsettled market conditions and customer uncertainty were expected to have a moderating effect on key markets in the near term.

In the first nine months of fiscal 2020, net cash from operating activities was $4.057 billion versus $404 million a year earlier, capital expenditures were $594 million versus $756 million, dividends paid were $718 million versus $703 million, the quarterly per-share dividend was held at $0.76, and share repurchases totaled $263 million versus $880 million a year earlier.

At August 2, 2020, total assets were $77.264 billion and total stockholders' equity was $12.891 billion (versus $73.011 billion and $11.417 billion at fiscal year-end 2019), with short-term borrowings of $9.075 billion, long-term borrowings of $34.037 billion, cash of $8.190 billion and marketable securities of $640 million.

Equipment Operations gross margin (net sales less cost of sales, divided by net sales) was approximately 25.8% in the third quarter of fiscal 2020, up from approximately 23.4% a year earlier, even as equipment sales volume fell.

Consolidated pretax income margin (total net sales and revenues minus total costs and expenses, divided by total net sales and revenues) rose to approximately 14.2% in the third quarter of fiscal 2020 from approximately 11.1% a year earlier.
Nine-month free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures) improved to approximately $3.463 billion in fiscal 2020 from approximately negative $352 million a year earlier.

repairs_needed: A reviewer wanting exact Q3 FY2020 XBRL-tagged consolidated operating income (as opposed to the derived pretax-margin figure used here) should pull it from Deere's Q3 FY2020 Form 10-Q once available; that filing postdates the Aug 21, 2020 press release used as this case's primary source and was not independently checked against XBRL because no XBRL facts exist for the 8-K itself.

Short-term (current) borrowings are only available at the Aug 2, 2020 point from the press release; the pre-cutoff XBRL extract for this issuer does not include a separate short-term/current debt tag, so the FY2016-FY2019 'prior' comparison for the net-debt headline metric uses long-term noncurrent debt only and is flagged as not fully comparable in that entry's definition.

No corporate-action/dividend ledger was available in this packet; per research/MVP_PROMPT.md's cross-case repair note, DE's in-window dividends should be added from the cached vendor events and marked vendor-data-pending once that ledger exists.

Financial figures for the Q3 FY2020 press release (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow detail) were extracted via three separate WebFetch parses of the same SEC exhibit rather than read from a local text copy; the figures cross-check internally (e.g., Agriculture & Turf plus Construction & Forestry net sales sum to the disclosed Equipment Operations total; the FY2019 fiscal year-end balance-sheet figures quoted in the release match the independently-sourced XBRL FY2019 10-K figures exactly), but a reviewer auditing exact figures should still verify against the filing text directly.
